items.title: 19.3.1 Models Proposed for the Mechanism of DNA Replication

source_refs.note: Topic 19.3.1 (PDF 123); Figure 19.8 is replaced by the original diagram.

blocks.text: Three models were proposed for the basic mechanism of DNA replication.

blocks.alt: Three columns of DNA molecules drawn as pairs of bars, old strands dark and new strands light, over two generations. Conservative: one all-old and one all-new molecule, then one all-old and three all-new. Semi-conservative: each daughter has one old and one new strand. Dispersive: every strand is a patchwork of old and new pieces.
blocks.caption: Three models over two generations (original diagram after Figure 19.8).
blocks.long_description: Three models were proposed. In the conservative model the parent double helix stays intact and a wholly new double helix is made, so one daughter has both old strands and the other both new strands. In the semi-conservative model the parent strands separate and each acts as a template for a new strand, so each daughter has one old and one new strand. In the dispersive model the parent DNA is broken up and old and new pieces are mixed in all the strands of the daughters.

blocks.caption: The three models
rows: The parent double helix stays intact and generates a new double helix made wholly of new material.
One has both parent strands; one has both new strands.
The two parent strands separate and each acts as a template for a new strand.
Each has one parent strand and one new strand.
The parent double helix is broken and dispersed into nucleotides, which combine with new nucleotides to make the four strands.
All strands are mixtures of old and new nucleotides.
